result.summary: The street features continuous sidewalks on both sides and parallel parking that narrows the travel lane, which likely helps to moderate vehicle speeds. However, the lack of marked crossings and the visual obstructions created by parked cars pose risks for pedestrians attempting to cross the roadway.

hazards.name: Parked Vehicle Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street creates a visual barrier between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the travel lane.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the visible block.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no visible marked crosswalks or designated crossing points within the immediate vicinity, forcing pedestrians to cross at unmarked locations.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) at the upcoming intersection to improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians and to shorten the crossing distance.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add high-visibility marked crosswalks at the intersection to provide a clear, designated path for pedestrians.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with row houses and a wide, paved sidewalk in good condition. A utility pole is located in the center of the walkway, creating a physical obstruction, and there is no buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A utility pole is positioned in the middle of the sidewalk, narrowing the clear path for pedestrians and mobility devices.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or planting strip between the sidewalk and the travel lane, increasing exposure to traffic.

interventions.title: Utility Pole Relocation
interventions.description: Relocate the utility pole to the edge of the sidewalk or into a furniture zone to provide a clear, unobstructed walking path.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planting Strips
interventions.description: Install street trees or a planting strip between the sidewalk and the curb to provide a physical and psychological buffer from traffic.

result.summary: The street features continuous sidewalks on both sides with a bus shelter on the right. While basic infrastructure like street lighting and marked crosswalks at the intersection are present, the environment lacks physical buffers between pedestrians and moving traffic on the left side.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars along the left curb block sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street along the row of buildings.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the left is directly adjacent to the parking/travel lane without a planting strip or furniture zone.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the intersection to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Upgrade the existing crosswalk markings to a high-visibility continental pattern.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Furniture Zone
interventions.description: Add a buffer zone with street trees or bollards on the left side to provide physical and psychological separation from traffic.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a continuous paved sidewalk in good condition, but it is severely compromised by utility poles placed directly in the walking path. The lack of a buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway, combined with the absence of traffic calming or marked crossings, reduces the overall safety and accessibility of the street.

hazards.name: Utility pole obstruction
hazards.description: Large wooden utility poles are situated in the middle of the sidewalk, significantly reducing the clear width and creating a major barrier for people with mobility aids.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the sidewalk in the foreground and mid-ground.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the roadway with no horizontal separation or vertical barriers to protect pedestrians from traffic.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening and Pole Relocation
interventions.description: Relocate utility poles to the edge of the right-of-way or underground them to provide a continuous, unobstructed clear path for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffer Zone
interventions.description: Install a planting strip with street trees between the sidewalk and the curb to provide physical separation and improve the pedestrian experience.
